$description: Jarvis theme tokens - the single source both clients' palettes are generated from (docs/HANDOFF-UI-RESEARCH-2026-10-09.md Phase B; the drift it retires is measured in docs/THEME-VALUE-PARITY-FINDINGS.md).
$schema_note: DTCG shape: a token is any node carrying $value; a group is any node without one; $type inherits down. Aliases are {group.token}. Values are exactly what a browser computes for the property, so a generated file and a checker can never disagree about `rgb(237, 241, 246)` versus `#edf1f6`.

meta.$description: Which generator owns which output, the mapping between the two clients' theme ids, and the CSS property names that are not derivable from a token name.

$themeIds.$description: Deliberate and already tested (jarvis-desktop/tests/continuity.mjs). The desktop ids are older, so a saved choice keeps working.

$cssNames.$description: Theme token -> CSS custom property, for the names a kebab rule would get wrong. Anything not listed kebabs (`accentBright` -> `--accent-bright`).

palette.$description: The spec's own ramps, as jarvis-visual-spec.json carries them. Held here because the phone's overrides name them, and the desktop's state tokens are these exact steps.

surface0.$description:
Reactor's blue-black - the HUD's --void / --plate / --plate-2 and the
     phone's Themes.REACTOR surface0-2 (#04070c, #0a1119, #0e1822) - at the
     alphas these see-through windows always had. They were a neutral
     grey-black before, so the spotlight, widget, Brain and Settings matched
     neither the HUD beside them nor the phone. Only the surfaces moved: the
     text colours below are tuned for transparent windows over any wallpaper
     and stay as they are.

surfaceSunken.$description:
Opaque, not translucent black. A sunken well at rgba(0,0,0,0.55) composites
     to light grey over a white desktop, and muted text on it measured 2.21:1 —
     the original CSS had exactly this bug. Making it solid means its contrast
     no longer depends on how many translucent parents it happens to sit
     inside, which is a property worth having when a component gets moved.

hairlineFocus.$description:
The one edge that carries meaning rather than decoration, so it is the one
     held to the 3:1 non-text floor. `--border` and `--border-strong` are
     separators; they are allowed to be quiet.

textHi.$description:
---- Text -------------------------------------------------------------
     `--text-faint` measured 2.37:1 over white in the old quickbar palette,
     which is unreadable on a light desktop. It is lifted here and the check
     holds it above 4.5:1 on both backdrops.

ok.$description:
---- Semantic ---------------------------------------------------------
     These four carry meaning, so a theme may retune them but must not swap
     what they mean. Every one of them is paired with a non-colour channel
     somewhere in the UI — a shape, a word or a position — because one man in
     twelve cannot tell `--ok` from `--warn`.

okFill.$description:
---- Semantic surfaces -------------------------------------------------
     A tinted fill and a legible text colour for each semantic state. These
     exist because components were reaching for `rgba(61,220,151,0.14)` and
     `#9ff0cc` directly — a green wash and a green text that a light theme
     could not touch, which is why Approve came out pale-on-pale on paper.

prose.$description:
---- Prose -------------------------------------------------------------
     A rendered answer is read for minutes at a time, so its body sits a shade
     below `--text` and its emphasis a shade above. Both were hex literals in
     `style.css`, which made a light theme render a model's answer in near-white
     on white.

codeBg.$description:
Code and diffs. A pure-black block is correct on a near-black theme and
     absurd on paper, so the ink and the ground are both tokens.

accentRgb.$description:
---- Raw channels ------------------------------------------------------
     The same colours as above, as bare `R G B` triples for `rgb(... / a)`.

     A component that needs a hue at 7% alpha had no token to reach for and
     wrote `rgba(56, 240, 255, 0.07)` — seventy-five such literals, each one a
     colour no theme could move. Adding seventy-five alpha-specific tokens
     would have been worse; this way the hue is the contract and the alpha
     stays where it is used, next to the thing it is tinting.

     `--sheen` and `--shade` are the two neutrals: the wash that LIFTS a
     surface and the one that SINKS it. On a dark theme the lift is white; on
     `paper` it is ink, which is the whole reason a component may not write
     `rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.05)` for a hover state. `--shade` stays dark
     everywhere — a drop shadow is a shadow on any theme.

nodeH1.$description:
FIVE hues, not ten, and a group is (hue x form) — see `drawNode` in
     brain.js. Ten hues cannot encode ten categories: the previous set measured
     CIEDE2000 6.0 between `core` and `cluster` in NORMAL vision and 1.0 under
     deuteranopia, and high-contrast gave those two the same value outright. A
     search over the whole HSL space found no ten that work, so the tenth
     channel is shape: five colours, each drawn as a filled disc or a hollow
     ring. Form survives greyscale, colour blindness and a 6px dot.

     These are search results, not picks. Every pair clears CIEDE2000 20 as the
     worst of normal, deuteranopia and protanopia, against a target of 15.
     Hand-tuning toward the spec's own families was tried and measured 1.7,
     because ice/indigo and amber/ember collide under CVD.

tag0.$description:
Chat tag colours (docs/CHAT-TAGS-DESIGN.md section 10; history-tags.js
     COLOURS): light ink for the dark themes, 4.5:1 or better on the tinted header. The header tint is the ink at 16% over the surface.

shadowCard.$description:
---- Depth -------------------------------------------------------------
     Self-drawn. Acrylic (`window-vibrancy`, windows.rs) genuinely blurs what
     is behind the quickbar, widget and HUD on a current Windows 11 machine -
     only its TINT colour is ignored above build 22523, where DWM takes over
     with its own transient backdrop colour instead (windows.rs
     `apply_quickbar_effects` has the detail). Brain, Settings and onboarding
     get no vibrancy at all: those windows are built opaque on purpose (the
     UI audit turned down a Mica backdrop for them, 2026-09-26), so `--shadow-pane`
     is their whole depth model, with nothing behind it to blur.

stateIdle.$description:
---- Face states -------------------------------------------------------
     The eight states the backend resolves, bound to the colours
     `jarvis-visual-spec.json` binds them to. These exist as tokens because
     without them a surface improvises: brain.css painted `listening` in
     `--warn`, which is amber — the colour the spec binds to APPROVAL — and had
     no rule for `approval` or `standby` at all, so both fell through to the
     base accent, which is what `speaking` uses. A missing state is now a
     missing token, and the token check can see it.

     `--state-standby` is the one declared divergence. The spec binds
     neutral-3 #46566a, which measures 2.03:1 on this window: fine for a face
     that fills a quarter of the screen and has its own rules, unreadable as a
     7px chrome dot against a 3:1 floor. #6b7d94 measures 3.61:1.

swatchReactorGround.$description:
---- Theme swatches ----------------------------------------------------
     The little preview beside each theme in Settings. Each shows THAT
     theme's ground and accent, whatever theme is showing, so these are the
     same in every theme block - which is why they live only here.

radiusWindow.$description:
---- Shape ------------------------------------------------------------
     A theme may change these. They are here so "cutting edge" can mean
     something structural — a sharper radius reads as a different product than
     a rounder one — rather than only meaning a different hue.

strokeHair.$description:
A WIDTH, and named so. It used to be `--hairline`, which is also the name
     `style.css` uses for a hairline COLOUR in 21 `border: 1px solid
     var(--hairline)` rules. The day style.css imports this file, every one of
     those would have become `border: 1px solid 1px` and silently vanished.
     `scripts/check-tokens.py` now fails on a name declared in two files.

text2xs.$description:
---- Type scale ---------------------------------------------------------
     Five sizes, standing in for about twenty near-duplicates that had drifted
     across style.css, widget.css, settings.css and brain.css (10, 10.5, 11,
     11.5, 12, 12.5, 13, 13.5px all meant "small label" or "compact body text"
     somewhere) - item 8, UI-AUDIT-2026-09-26.md. `--text-sm` is also the
     floor: nothing that protects or warns the owner is set below it.

     Left OUTSIDE this scale, deliberately: the prompt textarea and Brain's
     big stat number (each a one-off display size, not body text), the
     voice-training sentence in settings.css (already commented as "the
     biggest thing in the box, so it can be read from a normal sitting
     distance"), and the markdown h1-h4 heading ramp in style.css - a real,
     already-consistent four-step hierarchy of its own, not loose drift.

ease.$description:
---- Motion -----------------------------------------------------------
     Durations and easings are tokens so a theme can be calmer or sharper, and
     so `prefers-reduced-motion` has one place to collapse them.
